Crafting...so many ideas that have to be crammed into one coherent system. I like the framework we used in season 3, and think it can be expanded and tweaked to be even better. 

Right now the feeling I want to portray is railroad tycoon. Gone are the days of hunched over a small desk making a potion of healing. This is the age of the rail barons! We should be crafting airships and cannons, personal gliders and steam engines. The world has gotten bigger and so should our crafting.

Those are both really good points. The first was an intentional design decision. I wanted there to be some resentment of the nobility. I wanted the nobles to have to force everyone to do things they didn't like. Give the nobles more money and more problems. I wasn't as involved as I was hoping to be in that development, so I feel that it fell a bit flat. I don't think I would want to put that negative responsibility on players next time. It didn't really live up to my hopes.

The second point was also a design choice. Adjudicating custom items is very fun, and a good outlet for collaborative creativity, but this crafting system was designed specifically to not have to do that. It takes a lot of time making sure you produce a power balanced item that does what the player hopes. I really like doing that, but in season 2, it felt too arbitrary as to what people got. For better or for worse, the loudest and most aggressive players ended up with with the most custom loot. The squeaky wheel gets the grease. This year, the goal was to make a system that pretty much could run itself. And I think it did that well. But I also know we can do better.

I would love to see a fleshed out custom crafting system that people could still work toward on their own. One with minimal DM oversight that can still be constrained enough not to break any power level caps. I'm definitely open to any ideas on how to accomplish that.

OK, Stock Market mechanics....

This will be old school stock market, only open during strict business hours. You have to place your order with the broker, and they will buy the stock for you. You only read about stock price changes in the financial section of the newspaper the next day.

I'm thinking that we script out a system of stock market price changes, and write a script that automatically adjusts prices. If that's too difficult, then we set all the prices ahead of time, and nothing the players do will really affect them. They would be driven by the story. It puts everything a bit on rails, but maybe we don't want the players shaping world events that we are not expecting.

Anyway, each day we publish a newspaper page with articles about the different events than went on during the day. We will need dozens of articles written for the players to comb through and try to speculate in the market.
If they play the game well, then they could make a lot of money. That money will then be used for buying large magical airships and trains.

for crafting in season 3, time was the limiting factor in crafting. That worked well because you can't ever get more time. For season 4 time should still be the limiting factor, but I want to make tiers of crafting.

Maybe magic item crafting is one tier and takes specialized magic components, and requires certain relationships with traders or boroughs. Vehicle crafting is another, and maybe war effort crafting is another.

War effort crafting: A nearby town is planning a rebellion, but needs weapons to do so. As a crafter you can spend your adventuring gold to secure weapons from a faction you are in good with. They will supply the weapons, and you will gain favor with that faction and the people you helped. This favor can be translated into actual mechanical advantage in the form of encounter level boons. For example, maybe you supply food to a group of elves, and they send a representative with a battery of spells to help out at your next encounter.
Or maybe they give you lembus bread that grants advantage or something.
There should be a set reward that is offered so that the players can use the crafting system no matter which tier of crafting they are working with.
So, each year I completely re-imagine the crafting system. This year, I'm leaning toward implementing AngryGM crafting https://theangrygm.com/series/crafting-crafting/

This system solves that, but will require that each creature in the bestiary has a list of crafting items that will "drop"
The interdependent system of last year was fun, but the setting isn't right for it this time around.

I also want to enable the crafting of vehicles and I think the AngryGM system can accommodate that pretty well. I'm also trying to integrate this with the stocks and commodities trading system I'm cooking up.
Those will covered in a system I'm calling macro-crafting. They will require relationships with bankers, non-liquid credit, and logistics challenges.
The Angry GM system will require a complete rework of all prices though. We won't be able to easily use "Sane Magic Prices", but if I can get it worked out, I think it will be very rewarding.

OK, my crafting goals are a bit ambitious this year. It will involve including crafting ingredients in loot though. I want to have each entry in the bestiary have crafting resources that drop. For example, a dragon drops dragon hide. Each creature we use should have something if it's relevant, as part of the treasure for each encounter.

I'm kicking around some ideas for crafting airships as well, but mostly it's going to be faction dependent. That is, players will have to gain favor with the factions to even be allowed to purchase airships. Favor can be gained through encounters and missions.

so a thought, but why not make a small table based on type (maybe 6 minor, 3 medium, 1 major possibilities might work so a d10, or move it to a % and have a ton of options) for every creature type.  Fiends table, humanoids table, undead, so forth.  then you have a number of rolls based on creature CR.  People with appropriate tool skills (tanning or cooking for instance) can have an extra roll if a dm says its appropriate

then you wouldn't need a full creature by creature rundown, instead just type by type.  Give subbosses and bosses specific bonus loot, possibly one of a kind stuff, or even the first of its kind (you could make tables get better each week, so for instance, dragon tooth might only become available after week 2, and the week 2 boss is the first drop of it guaranteed)

it keeps much of the flavor your aiming for, with only a fraction of the work, and is mechanics us video game nerds are used to.  in fact, slip in a bards tale like joke about loot (<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RZl9KcSywos>) and you even have a handwave for something odd dropping from a critter (how did the tarrasque drop chitin... cause video game mechanics)

just an idea
